text:
Alex: Heads up — PR #19871 (reduce long-tail latency in seq-queue) is ready for merge but there's a DB cutover scheduled at 13:00 UTC. Can we decide whether to land now with a canary or wait for the rebase window?
Sana: @Alex what's the CI queue look like? if it's >30m we should probably avoid landing into the cutover window.
Alex: CI queue shows ~22m right now but runs are flaky on windows. commit: `c3f2a9b` — change is small (batching tweak). I can rebase quickly if needed.
ci-bot: CI status: linux/fast ✅, macos/e2e ⏳ (ETA ~18m), windows/integration ❌ (flake). Tests rerun triggered by @alex.
Mike: If the change is non-db schema and behind a flag, we could land a canary targeting 5% traffic first, then rollback if anything odd during cutover. Cutover ops prefers no schema changes during that hour.
Jen: I can be on pager during the cutover window. If we do a canary we should ensure the rollout is throttled and we have a quick rollback plan.
Alex: it's config-only, no schema touch. Feature flag `perf_opt_v2` present. Canary seems fine to me. I want to avoid blocking other PRs though.
Sana: Rebase slot available at 12:30 UTC for 15m. If @alex can rebase and get green by 12:50 we can do a small canary at 12:55 and then hold full rollout until after 13:30 (post-cutover).
Mike: +1 to that plan. Also add a deploy-bot guard: `--max-inflight 1 --concurrency 5%` for the rollout.
deploy-bot: Deploy plan prepared: PR #19871 -> canary (5%) at 12:55 UTC, monitor 10m, then escalate to 100% after 13:30 UTC if no errors. Rollback command: `deploy rollback pr-19871`.
Jen: I'll watch the canary and be ready to rollback. @alex ping me if you kick it off.
Alex: Rebase done, kicked CI. windows flake retried, now passing on second run. All green at 12:48 UTC. Kicking canary now (12:55 ETA).
ci-bot: All CI checks passed at 1718675328.
Sana: Thanks everyone. We'll follow the deploy-bot playbook and hold full rollout until post-cutover.
Jen: Canary is holding at 5% — no errors in first 6m. continuing to monitor.
Alex: resolved for now — canary live, full ramp post-cutover. I'll update the PR thread with the timeline. :thumbsup:
Mike: good coordination, nice work.
